title: Viral Obscura tweet — Rust agent browser at 30MB RAM, Puppeteer-compatible
summary: High-reach Spanish-language amplification of Obscura: claims a Rust headless browser for agents using 30MB RAM, 85ms loads, built-in anti-detect, native rendering without Chromium, and Puppeteer/Playwright compatibility; self-reply links the GitHub repo.
question_it_answers: What performance and anti-detect claims drove Obscura's viral agent-browser tweet?

claims.text: Tweet claims Obscura consumes 30MB RAM, loads pages in 85ms, and blocks 3,500+ trackers automatically.
claims.evidence:
> Consume 30MB de RAM
> Las paginas cargan en 85ms
> Bloquea +3.500 trackers automaticamente
claims.subject: mcp-and-agent-browsers

claims.text: Author positions Obscura as a direct Puppeteer and Playwright replacement with no Node.js dependencies in one binary.
claims.evidence:
Es un reemplazo directo de Puppeteer y Playwright

Sin Nodejs. Sin dependencias. Un solo binario
claims.subject: mcp-and-agent-browsers

claims.text: Immediate self-reply points to github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura as the repo behind the claims.
claims.subject: mcp-and-agent-browsers

claims.text: Local 0.2.1 serve RSS is 25,108 KB idle, 37,856 KB with example.com, and 73,080 KB with tinyshelf.co — above the tweet's 30 MB RAM line. Do not treat 30 MB as a page-loaded session.
claims.evidence: Idle 25108 kB; example.com CDP 37856 kB; tinyshelf CDP 73080 kB. README/tweet 30 MB not collapsed. See obscura NOTES.
claims.subject: mcp-and-agent-browsers

media.description: README crop showing Obscura wordmark, Trendshift number-one badge, and comparison table versus headless Chrome on memory, binary size, anti-detect, and page-load metrics.

judge_hints.why_must_read: Viral claim-source tweet with self-reply repo link; reconcile hype lines against README capture.
